html:
The arrival in 635 of Alopen, a monk of the Church of the East, at Chang'an, capital of the Tang dynasty. He is the first recorded Christian missionary to reach China.

He was probably a Syriac speaker from Persia, then under the Sasanian Empire, or from Syria, and he came along the Silk Road with scriptures. Emperor Taizong received him well, had his books translated in the palace library, and in 638 issued an edict allowing the faith to be taught. A monastery was built in the capital. The Tang court was open to foreign religions, and Chang'an was one of the most cosmopolitan cities in the world.

All we know of Alopen comes from the Xi'an Stele, a stone set up in 781 that tells the story of the church in China in Chinese and Syriac. Jesuits found it around 1625 and were delighted by its proof of early Christians in China. Chinese Christian texts of the time present the faith with Buddhist and Taoist words.

The church grew for two centuries, see Christians in Tang China, until the persecution of foreign religions in 845 all but ended it.
